page.layout: One page of running text, one column, no margin notes. Running head and page number at the top. Below the text, a small signature mark "o 4". Below that, a fleuron ornament (not transcribed).

p.i: denus, ut si quam in bello pecuniolam collegerint, ne rubiginem forte illa obducat, illico hospitibus committantur.

main_text.p: XII. Itaque etiam atque etiam te hortor: ut omni abiecta cogitatione militiae studia tua perse-quaris, quae & voluptates veras ac diuturnas habent: & deniq; bona ea adferunt, quae nec eripi, nec surripi possunt.

XIII. Loco natus es nobili, quem maxime virtus atque doctrina ornat: principem habes, & literatum ipsum, & summum literatorum patronum: parentes tibi Deus est largitus, qui suppeditare tibi sumptus, & volunt & possunt: nō ingenium deest: non alia ad capessenda studia necessaria desiderātur.
XIIII. Tuum igitur erit considerare potius, quid Deo, quid parentibus, quid cognatis & amicis debeas: quàm alij suadeant homines, non ad quietem atq; otium, sed bella nati.

page.notes: Italic and roman type were judged from the scan; the lead-in words of each numbered paragraph (XII, XIII, XIIII) and "Tuum igitur erit considerare potius," appear roman, the rest italic. The first word "denus" is read as printed (possibly "denuo"), and "quàm" may carry an accent, both uncertain. The ampersand "&" is printed as an Et-ligature and is written as "&". Long s is written as plain s throughout. The signature "o 4" sits mid-page below the text rather than at the foot, so it is marked [?]. The fleuron ornament is not text and is not transcribed.
